title: Skilled Worker visa: Knowledge of English - GOV.UK

content.p: You’ll usually need to prove your knowledge of the English language when you apply. You can prove it in one of the following ways, by:

content.li: having a degree from a UK institution
having a degree from an institution that was outside the UK and taught in English
passing an English test from an approved provider

content.p: If you have already proved your knowledge of English in a previous successful visa application, you may not have to prove it again.

content.h2: If you have a UK school qualification

content.p: You can prove your knowledge of English if you have a qualification from a UK school that you began when you were under 18. You must have one of the following qualifications:

content.li: Scottish Higher or Advanced Higher in English

content.h2: If you have a degree from a UK institution

content.p: You can prove your knowledge of English if you have a degree-level qualification that was both:

content.li: awarded by a UK institution, even if you studied outside the UK

content.h2: If you have a degree from an institution outside the UK

content.p: If your degree was taught in English and was not awarded by a UK institution, you’ll need to apply for an assessment from Ecctis .
Ecctis will give you a code to confirm that your qualification is equivalent to a UK bachelor’s degree or higher and was taught in English.
If you do not have any qualifications that prove your knowledge of English, you will need to pass a Secure English Language Test (SELT) with an approved provider.
You must prove you can read, write, speak and understand English to at least level B2 on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages ( CEFR ) scale .

content.h3: If you’re extending, updating or switching your visa

content.p: If you had this visa before 8 January 2026 and you’re applying to extend or update it, you need level B1 English. You do not need to prove your knowledge of English again.
If you’re switching from a Health and Care Worker visa, you also do not need to provide proof again.
If you’re applying to switch from a different visa, you need level B2.

content.h2: Who does not need to prove their knowledge of English

content.p: You do not need to prove your knowledge of English if you’re a national of one of the following countries or territories:

content.h3: If you’re a doctor, dentist, nurse, midwife or vet

content.p: You do not need to prove your knowledge of English if you’ve already passed an English Language assessment that is accepted by the relevant regulated professional body.
If you’re a vet, you may need to prove that you passed an English Language assessment with the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons.
